title: Signal tiling and narrative bridge for low-bandwidth time-series
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers embed high-cardinality time-series charts into low-bandwidth contexts (mobile, satellite links, embedded consoles). Current chart rendering sends full-series payloads and eagerly hydates tooltips/legends which leads to long first-paint, janky interactions, and inaccessible summaries for screen-reader users when data is sparse or heavily downsampled.

Goal: Design a unified interaction and visual protocol that: 1) progressively surfaces high-fidelity data as bandwidth/CPU permits, 2) provides a concise, screen-reader-first narrative summary immediately on mount (the 'narrative bridge'), and 3) prioritizes legend/tooltip interactions to reduce client-side work while preserving discoverability. We should reuse existing design tokens (color/spacing/motion) and produce a pattern that engineering can implement with streaming tiles and a sampling fallback.

Proposed solution overview:
- Signal tiling: Break long sequences into coarse tiles (time windows) that load in increasing fidelity. Initial tile = aggregated quantiles + spike markers; subsequent tiles fetch denser samples. Visual cue (micro-gradient on x-axis) indicates loading progress.
- Narrative bridge (SR-first): On initial render, show a compact text summary generated from the aggregation tile (e.g., "Last 24h: steady at 42–47 units, one spike at 03:12 UTC"). This summary is announced via aria-live and available in the legend area as a persistent collapsed paragraph for keyboard/screen-reader users.
- Legend prioritization: Enable a 'relevance first' legend sort computed from recent activity; in low-bandwidth mode show only the top 3 series by delta and provide an overflow menu that lazy-loads the rest. Tooltips are inert until the tile containing the hovered timepoint is loaded — showing a lightweight placeholder with approximate values and an affordance to request the full sample.
- Token usage: Map the three fidelity states to tokenized motion and opacity tokens (motion-medium, motion-none), and a dedicated low-fidelity color token (chart.lowContrastFill). Spacing tokens control the collapsed narrative block and legend overflow spacing.

Design artifacts required:
- Figma prototype with three fidelity states, legend overflow behavior, and SR narrative block.
- Interaction spec documenting network + UI sequence diagrams (initial tile -> progressive fetch -> full hydration).
- Accessibility notes with aria attributes, announcement timing, and keyboard flows.
- Performance acceptance criteria and suggested telemetry hooks (first-paint-for-chart, tiles-loaded-time, tooltip-hydration-latency).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Visual: initial chart renders within 300ms on simulated 3G with aggregated tile and narrative bridge visible.
2) Accessibility: screen readers announce the narrative bridge within 600ms of mount; keyboard users can expand the narrative, tab to legend overflow, and open a tooltip with keyboard-only controls.
3) Perf: progressive tiles finish loading for the visible viewport within 2s under simulated typical mobile conditions; placeholder tooltips never block main thread for >50ms.
4) Tokens: implementation uses approved tokens for color, motion, and spacing; new tokens proposed for low-fidelity must be documented and minimal.

Trade-offs considered:
- Prefetch vs on-demand: prefetching more tiles reduces perceived latency but increases network cost; recommendation: prefetch one adjacent tile only.
- Narrative verbosity: shorter narratives read faster for SR but may omit key signals; default to concise summary with a discoverable 'details' expansion.
- Legend trimming: hiding series reduces cognitive load on mobile but may obscure important signals; show delta-sorted top items with clear overflow.

Implementation dependencies: ENG-48210 (runtime: tiled-series endpoint), ENG-48921 (client: tooltip hydration API), ENG-49105 (analytics: chart telemetry).

QA checklist:
- Simulate 2G/3G throttling and verify narrative announcement and initial tile render timings.
- Keyboard-only navigation through legend overflow and narrative expand/collapse.
- Screen reader walkthrough (NVDA, VoiceOver) verifying announcement timing and focus behavior.
- Contrast audit for new low-fidelity color token.

Notes for engineers: include sample payload shapes in the interaction spec (aggregation buckets with percentile summaries + spike markers) and a minimal client API for requesting tile upgrades for a given viewport range. Prefer an opt-in flag (chart.fidelityMode = "progressive") to avoid regressing existing consumers.
comments: 2025-02-14: Kickoff meeting with PM and Design Systems. Agreed scope: narrative bridge + tiling + legend overflow. Action: Asha to prototype microcopy; Lin to align tokens with theme team.
2025-02-16: Sketches reviewed — PM asked for a compact fallback when the narrative expansion collides with small viewports. Added an affordance to collapse legend into an icon-only mode.

2025-02-18: UX research session with two developer customers who embed dashboards in mobile webviews. Feedback: they prefer explicit 'show full data' control rather than automatic hydration in metered contexts. We will expose the control in the legend overflow.

2025-02-19: Reviewed with Accessibility lead (Samir Rao). Action items: ensure aria-live region is resumable and include read-once vs persistent modes per customer preference. Also check focus order for keyboard nav.
2025-02-21: Prototype in Figma linked; ready for handoff to frontend pair for spike implementation. Plan for a 2-week engineering spike to validate telemetry and baseline times under throttling.
Design note: propose a single new token 'chart.lowFidelityAccent' with a2 contrast to background; team to decide at token grooming on 2025-02-25.
